newsitem.title: USA: Parts of Fla citrus belt wet from hurricane rains.
newsitem.headline: Parts of Fla citrus belt wet from hurricane rains.

text.p: The interior and upper areas of the Florida citrus belt received very little rain during the week ended October 20, but Hurricane Lili supplied the southern and coastal regions with ample precipitation, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.

"Low pressure from the north and feeder bands from Hurricane Lili supplied the southern and coastal parts of the citrus belt with plenty of moisture this week," FASS said in its weekly weather and crop news report.
Weekly temperatures averaged within a degree or two of normal, with lows in the 40s and 50s (Fahrenheit) in the north. Highs remained in the 80s (Fahrenheit).
Some young trees are still producing new growth, and harvest is increasing as more crops pass maturity tests, FASS said.
